newsitem.title: INDIA: India's TELCO net races past forecasts.
newsitem.headline: India's TELCO net races past forecasts.

text.p: India's leading truckmaker Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company (TELCO) on Tuesday beat market expectations when it announced a whopping 44 percent increase in net profit for the year ended March 31, 1997.
TELCO said its net profit surged to 7.62 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), from 5.3 billion in the previous year.
"It's a brilliant result on the face of it," said Anupam Thareja, analyst at HSBC B&K Securities.
TELCO shares jumped 11 rupees, or nearly three percent, to 404 in after-hours kerb deals in Bombay. The stock had closed 7.0 rupees lower at 393 in official trade on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Automobile analysts -- who had pegged their 1996/97 net profit forecasts at around 7.2 billion rupees -- said a lower tax rate had boosted profits.
"The key area I had underestimated was taxation," said K.N. Sreenivasan, automobile analyst at Jardine Fleming India Broking. "I had assumed the tax rate to be around 29 percent."
TELCO said its effective rate of tax was 24 percent in 1996/97, compared to 30 percent in the previous year.
"Taxation was the key reason for the higher than expected profits," said analyst Kapil Krishan at Peregrine Capital India.
TELCO said company profits before and after tax rose by 32 percent and 44 percent respectively.

"The company was able to achieve this despite a slackening in the offtake of vehicles in the domestic market in the second half due to tighter credit, drop in freight rates on road transport and the slowdown in economic growth," TELCO said in a statement.

Lower demand for vehicles forced most automobile firms to slash production in the past year. TELCO's output in 1996/97 was 218,393 units, according to figures released by the Association of Indian Automobile Manufacturers.
TELCO had announced a production target of around 240,000 units during roadshows for its $200 million issue of global equity in calendar 1996.
The company said in its results statement vehicle sales climbed 19 percent to 215,261 units. It did not release its production figures.
Analysts said an improvement in operating margins also boosted the firm's 1996/97 net.
"There is a 0.4 percent improvement at the operating level which is good for a company this size," Thareja said.
Peregrine's Krishan said margins were up against the general expectation of weaker margins due to the recent industrial slowdown.
He said he expected TELCO's net profit to rise by around 10 percent to 8.44 billion rupees in 1997/98, on a tax rate of 25 percent.
"The stock is bound to rise tommorrow," Jardine's Sreenivasan said. "But once the initial euphoria is over investors will look towards the oil price hike which is round the corner."
The government is discussing raising the price of oil products to cut a mushrooming subsidy bill.
